items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: He was in my band for a long time.

ctx.x: I see. Yeah. I remember. We talked about that. In fact, the next person on the list is Israel Crosby.

Huh! That's a coincidence. Well, Israel Crosby was one of the greatest bass players, not only in my estimation, but in the estimation of most of the musicians that heard him, really, one of the greatest bass players that ever played the bass. In fact, as small as the guy was, you know he could play tuba and all that stuff. He played a little bit of that with Fletcher. He was in my band for a long time. Then He joined Fletcher's band at the Grand Terrace, and that was during the Christopher Columbus theme song…

In fact, our rhythm section consisted of Israel Crosby on bass, Big Sid Catlett (inaudible) on drums; a guy named Bobby Lessee from Brooklyn, New York, was guitarist. We had three. Another one that followed him in later years that I think was at the Grand Terrace was Lawrence Lucie, who we talked about, and Bernard Addison, who was an excellent swing man, like Charlie Christian, something like Charlie Christian, I should say. I'll modify that, because I love Charlie.
